interpretation: Large absolute Spearman correlations indicate overlapping information; they do not by themselves prove harmful multicollinearity.
Very low variation or few unique values can limit the information available to a model.
A prediction/actual SD ratio far below 1 indicates compressed predictions; interpret alongside calibration slope and correlation.
A slope far below 1 indicates predictions vary less than actual outcomes; a slope near 1 is not sufficient without low error.
A high gap between median and 90th-percentile receiver MAE indicates performance may be uneven across players.
Differences across draft cohorts are descriptive, especially with the 2025 held-out cohort of 14 receivers.
Repeated selection of the largest alpha suggests the tested grid may not bracket the optimum or the predictors carry weak signal. It is not proof of a coding error.
These observational predictions do not establish that Combine traits cause in-game movement performance.
